23 For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God; 24 Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus: (Romans 3:23-24 KJV)

This verse makes it clear that we all have sinned and come short of being like Jesus (the glory of God). Since we are all sinners, and in the same boat, we should all realize that no matter how good we try to be, we can never earn our salvation. The people that think they are good enough on their own, that God will accept them without Jesus, are just deceived, as they are sinners as this verse says, and therefore will not be allowed into the presence of God (John 14:6). It is amazing that so many churches still try to teach that God looks upon what you do, and how you act, to see if you are holy enough for Him to bless you. If God didn’t use a dirty vessel, He wouldn’t have anyone to use, as we are all defiled when compared to Jesus (Isaiah 54:6).

All us sinners have had the Grace of God appear to us (Titus 2:11), and all people can be justified freely by this Grace. This doesn’t mean that all will be saved, as you have to put faith in the grace of God to be saved (Ephesians 2:8). It takes faith in Jesus for salvation. Notice that it is freely given, and not something to be earned. Religion teaches all of us, that we have to live holy, go to church, read the bible, and do all kinds of works of the law, for God to fellowship or bless us, and that is not what the bible teaches. Pastors need to study the Word, and realize that it teaches that we are saved by the grace of God freely, and that we are to walk in the same way that we were saved (Colossians 2:6). We need to teach the love of God and not works, as that is what the Gospel of Christ is all about. The “Good News” of the Gospel of Jesus Christ, is that it is what He has done for us, and not what we do for Him, that saves us. Just believe in Jesus, and you will be saved, then obey Him to assure your eternal salvation (Hebrews 5:9). Thank you Jesus for our salvation!
